task_description: Elementwise y = x*scale+bias over a (512, 128) bf16 array, processed in 4 row-blocks via pltpu.emit_pipeline, comparing no_pipelining=True (fully synchronous copy/compute/copy per block) against the default no_pipelining=False (automatic double-buffered overlap).

metrics.name: dma_wait_fraction
metrics.description: fraction of total kernel time spent waiting on HBM<->VMEM DMA rather than computing. This is the metric that actually distinguishes naive from optimized here -- unlike 02_vmem_tile_layout/03_vectorized_vmem, there is no exact code-level fact (like a grid-step count) that proves the difference; it's a genuine runtime overlap behavior. Requires a real profiler trace to observe (agent/profiler.py, not yet implemented) -- eval.py's current TFLOPS/median_ms numbers are a weaker proxy (a real overlap benefit should show up as lower median_ms for the same total data movement).

known_gotcha: emit_pipeline queries real TPU tiling info even under interpret=True and raises on a non-TPU host unless wrapped in jax.sharding.use_abstract_mesh with an AbstractDevice naming a TPU generation (see naive_kernel.py's _ABSTRACT_TPU_V5E). Undocumented in the obvious places; found by hitting the error and reading jax/_src/tpu_info.py.
